name: @vishwanko-9/vi-torrent
description: A BitTorrent client that lives in the terminal, built on @opentui + SolidJS + WebTorrent, running on Bun.
author: vishwako-9
//files: Ships the BUILT dist/, not raw src/. Bun ignores a package's tsconfig.json for files under node_modules - it assumes a published package is already compiled - so publishing .tsx meant a global install died instantly with "Cannot find module 'react/jsx-dev-runtime'". Verified by installing the real tarball globally. The 4 screenshots are listed individually rather than shipping the whole docs/ folder - the README needs only these, and the rest of docs/ is markdown nobody installing the package needs bundled.
//preinstall: npm installs this happily and says nothing, then `npm start` dies with a bare 'bun is not recognized'. engines.bun does not help - npm only validates the node and npm keys, even with engine-strict. This stops it at the first command instead, with a message that names the actual requirement. It must invoke bun rather than node: bun ships no node shim, so anyone who followed the README has bun and no node.

scripts.preinstall: bun --version || (echo vi-torrent needs Bun, not Node - install it from https://bun.sh and see the README: https://github.com/vishwako-9/vi-torrent#prerequisites && exit 1)
scripts.build: bun build src/index.tsx src/daemon.ts --outdir dist --target bun --packages external

//trustedDependencies: Bun blocks dependency lifecycle scripts unless listed here. node-datachannel's install script fetches its prebuilt WebRTC binary; without it a fresh `bun install` produces a client that dies on startup with 'Cannot find module build/Release/node_datachannel.node'. Deliberately NOT trusting the rest: bufferutil and utf-8-validate are optional ws speedups, utp-native is an optional webtorrent dependency, and ip-set's preinstall runs `npx only-allow pnpm`, which would fail the install outright.
//platforms: No os restriction. Windows and Linux are both verified - full suite plus a real launch on each. macOS is UNTESTED (no machine), but uses the same POSIX path as Linux. The old win32 restriction existed because utp-native panics on POSIX under Bun; that is now handled in src/webtorrent-platform.ts by disabling uTP off Windows.
